title: Palindrome From Two-Letter Words

concept.title: Pair every word with its reversal
body: Each word has exactly two letters. When you write chosen words one after another to form a palindrome, a word `xy` placed in the first half must be matched by the word `yx` in the mirror position of the second half. So words come in **pairs `xy` and `yx`**. A word with two **equal** letters, such as `aa`, is its own reversal: two copies of it form a pair, and **one single leftover copy** can stand in the centre.

Every pair contributes 4 letters (2 words of 2 letters). Only one word can be in the middle, so the centre bonus of 2 letters is added at most once, however many words `aa`, `bb`, ... have a leftover.

statement: You are given `n` words of exactly two lowercase letters. Choose some of them (each word at most once) and write them in a row, in any order, so that the resulting text is a palindrome. Print the greatest possible length of such a text (0 if no word can be used).
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` words.
constraints: Each word has exactly 2 lowercase letters.

examples.input:
6
lc cl gg gg ab ba
examples.note: The pairs lc + cl, ab + ba and gg + gg give 4 letters each: 12 in total.
ty + yt form a palindrome of length 4.

hints: A word `xy` needs a partner `yx` on the other side of the palindrome.
For `x != y` take `min(count[xy], count[yx])` pairs, each pair gives 4 letters.
Words like `aa` pair with themselves; one leftover `aa` may go in the centre (+2).

input = sys.stdin.readline

solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).
